rows.detail: noted in the register as “Lt in the Royal Engineers”
rows.means: Connolly's Roll says he died at Chatham on 6 May 1805. Buried three days later, and the parish clerk knew his rank.

rows.detail: spinster · married John Maddock JONES, Esq., bachelor, of Penybryn in the parish of Ruabon, Denbighshire · by licence · witnesses JOSEPH D'ARCY and Richd Lovett
rows.means: Robert and Jean's daughter, married at twenty-five. The witness is her brother Joseph — the child baptised at Portsea in 1780.
Not Robert's son but George's — by his first wife. The surveyor, and the half-brother the archive has written about without a record for him.
Jean Ward, dead at sixty-six. An age of 66 in March 1823 puts her birth about 1756 — the tree says 1754.

rows.detail: father GEORGE PITT D'ARCY, “Bt: Major 39th Foot” · mother MARIA · abode Chatham
rows.means: The Major himself, in a parish register, with his rank and regiment. His daughter was christened on 31 March 1826 — and the convict ship England embarked his detachment eight days later.

Major-General Robert D'Arcy, C.B. Connolly gives his death as 13 May 1827; he was buried six days later. An age of 76 puts his birth about 1750–51 — and this is the register the tree's “1751” has always come from, seen at last.
A child, and no connection to this family has been shown. Listed because she is in the record.
